At the EDUCAUSE annual conference, Google.org announced its support of three higher education initiatives to scale ethical AI readiness, modernize institutional planning, and expand student success.

Editor’s note: This week we’re joining thousands of faculty and administrators at EDUCAUSE , one of the United States’ biggest higher education technology exhibitions. Visit us at Booth #700 , where you can see demos of Gemini for Education, Gemini Notebook, and the latest Google Cloud AI solutions. Follow along on X and Facebook for the latest updates.

As higher education leaders gather this week at the EDUCAUSE Annual Conference , AI is undoubtedly top of mind for all. While this technology offers significant opportunities to support students, faculty, and staff, many institutions — especially community colleges and public university systems — face resource constraints. Recent studies indicate that 41% of higher-ed educators say they have not received any formal training on using AI tools in learning environments.

To help close this gap, Google.org is supporting two higher education initiatives focused on keeping educators at the heart of using AI:

## Supporting adult learners

Despite making up at least a third of higher education enrollments for decades, adult learners 25 and older are more likely to drop out , returning for their second year at a rate 35 percentage points lower than traditional-age students.

To address systemic barriers for these students, the Coalition of Urban Serving Universities (USU), in partnership with the Association of Public and Land-grant Universities (APLU) , is enhancing its Urban Adult Learner Institute (UALI).

Supported by Google.org, USU is integrating Grow with Google resources and AI-integrated lessons into its professional development certification. By equipping higher education practitioners, including faculty and advisors, with practical, hands-on tasks, schools can offer students better career guidance and help them succeed. Educators across 30 universities will test these new methods so other schools can easily replicate what works to ensure success for adult learners.

## Creating new models for career-connected learning

While traditional internships have long been the standard for career readiness, overwhelming demand from students and employers has created a need for scalable new approaches.

To meet this moment, USU is leading a project to scale career-focused community-based learning (CBL) enhanced by AI. Over the next 15 months, USU will collect and qualitatively analyze 10 models at member institutions, publish case studies, and convene a working group to develop a research and practice agenda. The initiative will create flexible work-based learning pathways across diverse academic disciplines, expanding workforce readiness for a wide range of students.

## Reimagining strategic planning

Strategic planning at community colleges is often treated as a compliance exercise rather than an engine for innovation. Through its Reimagining Community Colleges (RCC) initiative, Education Design Lab (The Lab) is helping two-year institutions transform that dynamic and prepare students for the future of work with support from Google.org.

Following a successful summit of educators this week and a cohort of five colleges launching redesign plans, a new national competition will launch in early 2027 for a state-level community college system to undergo a two-year initiative to use technology-enabled solutions to better serve their students. This upcoming phase will apply The Lab’s Future of Learning framework to build scalable, durable solutions that strengthen continuous innovation across campuses.

To explore free training resources and learn more about our education initiatives, visit the Google for Education Learning Center or connect with our teams this week at EDUCAUSE.

# Google's AI ranks #1 for predicting flu hospitalizations.

Zahra Shamsi

Google Research

Sep 30, 2026

A flu forecasting model built with Google AI was the best at forecasting flu-related hospital admissions during the 2025-26 season, the Centers for Disease Control announced this week .

From October through May, the CDC’s FluSight combines weekly submissions from government, industry, and academic teams predicting U.S. hospital admissions for the current week and three weeks into the future. The CDC uses the combined forecast each week to communicate the anticipated state-level demand for medical services.

The end-of-season analysis published this week shows that of 39 eligible models, Google’s best matched the season’s observed hospital admissions. This performance validates our confidence that AI combined with human ingenuity will improve our ability to forecast diseases worldwide.

Google forecasts were developed using Empirical Research Assistance , an AI tool that generates optimization algorithms across a range of scientific fields. Research on ERA was recently published in the journal “Nature.” ERA’s underlying technology is now available to trusted testers as part of our experimental science tools .

# Guided Vision in Gemini Live: built for accessibility

Oct 01, 2026

- x.com

- Facebook

Built alongside the blind and low-vision community, Guided Vision in Gemini Live offers conversational, real-time visual assistance. Share your camera to receive dynamic audio descriptions and natural verbal reframing cues to explore your environment.

Isha Sheth

Senior Product Manager, Gemini Live

Today, we’re launching Guided Vision in Gemini Live across compatible Android devices — bringing voice-forward, real-time visual interpretation to people who are blind, have low vision, or want intuitive visual assistance.

Technology is most powerful when it opens up the world for everyone, and Guided Vision turns Gemini into a conversational visual partner. Guided Vision was developed through close collaboration with the accessibility community. We previewed it earlier this month, among other tools to expand digital and physical accessibility across Android,

To train Gemini Live for conversational, real-world context, we partnered with Aira to visually interpret data for a total of tens of thousands of hours. More than 1,000 members of Aira’s Trusted Tester network helped stress-test and refine the model across daily routines, while Aira specialists worked directly with our teams as subject-matter experts to help establish and evaluate our safety guardrails.

Now, you can simply share your camera during a Gemini Live session to hear clear descriptions of your surroundings, ask detailed follow-up questions, and receive proactive, spoken cues to center whatever you want to explore.

## Real-time visual assistance designed for how you experience the world

When you share your camera in Gemini Live with Guided Vision turned on, Gemini acts as a conversational partner. If your camera is pointed too high, too close, or slightly off to the side, Gemini provides natural verbal prompts to help you reframe — asking you to pan slowly to the right, tilt downward, or step back so it can get the clear visual context needed to answer your questions.

## Everyday moments made simple

Whether locating objects, preparing a meal, or picking an outfit, Guided Vision supports everyday tasks where quick visual verification matters most:

- Reading fine print and complex text : Read small nutrition labels on food packages, decipher appliance dials and washing machine cycles, or read printed menus in dimly lit restaurants.

- Finding and localizing objects: Search your immediate area for everyday items, such as finding a dropped earbud on the floor or locating the black pepper inside a crowded spice cabinet.

- Describing objects and matching details: Ask about colors, patterns, and shapes — such as checking whether a striped shirt pairs with a pair of trousers or identifying the color of a specific jacket.

- Exploring your immediate environment : Get descriptive overviews of unfamiliar spaces, room layouts, or objects placed across a table.

- Conversing naturally in your preferred language: Guided Vision supports conversations across multiple languages. It reflects extensive testing and feedback from blind and low-vision communities across India, Brazil, Singapore, Indonesia, Japan, and more to make descriptions, reframing cues, and answers feel natural and helpful.

Like many accessibility innovations, Guided Vision also provides practical visual assistance for older adults, individuals with low literacy, or anyone trying to read fine print in low lighting.

## Quick access across Android

Guided Vision is designed to fit seamlessly into daily routines with minimal friction:

- Gemini App : Open your profile settings in the Gemini mobile app and switch on Use Guided Vision in Live . From there, open Gemini Live and tap to share your camera.

- Accessibility Shortcuts : Under Android Settings > Accessibility > Vision assistance > Guided Vision, configure an Accessibility shortcut to launch Guided Vision using the floating accessibility button, a two-finger swipe gesture, or by pressing both volume keys.

- TalkBack Integration : Users running Google TalkBack can bring up the TalkBack menu with a three-finger tap and select Guided Vision directly.

As with any generative AI technology, Guided Vision is an assistive utility and can make mistakes. It is not a medical device, mobility aid, or white cane replacement, and it’s not intended for navigation, safe-travel guidance, or obstacle detection. Users should continue relying on established mobility aids and safe-travel practices in physical environments.

Guided Vision is now available on Android devices running Android 9 and above in regions and languages where Gemini Live is supported. Make sure your Gemini app and Android system software are updated to the latest versions to get started.

For more than 20 years, we’ve invested in machine learning and AI research, tools, and infrastructure to build products that make everyday life better for more people. Teams across Google are working on ways to unlock AI’s benefits in fields as wide-ranging as healthcare, crisis response, and education. To keep you posted on our progress, we're doing a regular roundup of Google's most recent AI news.

Here’s a look back at some of our AI announcements from September.

September's headline belongs to Gemini 4 Argon, our newest frontier model. Built with advanced reasoning and a 1-million-token context window, it’s designed to tackle complex challenges — especially in cybersecurity defense. The release capped an active month for Google AI launches that included Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber. We also introduced expressive voice models with Gemini 3.8 Live, made Googlebook available for pre-order, and brought the Gemini app to Windows. Beyond daily tools, we marked major scientific milestones by mapping human DNA in AlphaGenome Atlas, tracking global methane from space, and launching Project Suncatcher to test machine learning hardware in orbit. And as a nice bonus, we were grateful to see our teams’ work on designing better AI interfaces recognized by Fast Company as the 2026 Design Company of the Year.

Learn about Gemini 4 Argon: our next era of frontier intelligence . Gemini 4 Argon is engineered to bring advanced reasoning to the most difficult of problems. Built with an industry-leading 1-million-token context window, Argon excels at heavy-duty workloads like coding, cybersecurity defense, and knowledge work like financial research and legal drafting, and autonomous cybersecurity patching. Safely releasing frontier capabilities at this level requires a phased approach, and Argon is currently rolling out to trusted cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program. We’re actively gathering feedback from early testers to iterate on guardrails before expanding availability to developers, enterprises, and consumers.

Get next-gen intelligence for agents and cybersecurity with Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber . Gemini 3.8 delivers our best reasoning and coding performance yet at the same speed and low cost as 3.7 Flash. Gemini 3.8 Flash provides substantial gains in long-horizon software engineering, multi-step problem solving, and agentic workflows. Alongside it, Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber equips defenders with frontier-grade autonomous vulnerability discovery and automated code patching — available to trusted organizations through our new Fairwind Program .

Converse naturally with Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking . We've launched two fast, natural language audio models: Gemini 3.8 Live for everyday conversation, and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, the top-rated speech-to-speech model for multi-step reasoning without all the lag. Both have rolled for developers in Google AI Studio and Gemini API , and for everyone across Search Live, Gemini Live, and Google Workspace, where you can get things done using your voice in Gmail, Docs, and Keep .

Say hello to Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS and Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS . Our most expressive text-to-speech models yet let you generate custom voices, direct scene dialogue, and more from simple text prompts. Instead of choosing from a fixed list of static presets, you now get a dynamic creative studio to build voice-first applications and elevate audio experiences, rolling out across products including Gemini Notebook and Google Vids.

Tackle tasks with new Connected Apps in Gemini . We brought more of your favorite apps directly into Gemini, including productivity tools like Airtable, Linear, monday.com, and PandaDoc; creative platforms including Adobe, Picsart, Squarespace, and Webflow; and lifestyle services such as Peloton, SeatGeek, and Experian. Instead of switching between tabs, you can now tackle your tasks all in one place. To get started, head to your Gemini settings and select the apps you want to link.

Create your best tracks yet with Lyria 3.5 in Gemini . From simple text prompts or images, you can now use our most expressive music generation model yet to produce richer arrangements, coherent songs, and personalized audio right in the Gemini app. Lyria 3.5 is available globally in Gemini and across Google AI Studio, Google Flow Music, and Google Vids.

Sharpen your study routine with new Gemini Notebook tools . Now you can transform your study routine in Gemini Notebook with interactive coursework tools and animated video summaries. Master complex topics using custom flashcards, versatile quiz formats, and 60-second Short Video Overviews in over 80 languages. For back-to-school season, eligible college students can also claim a free 12-month Google AI student plan with higher usage limits.

Coordinate family life effortlessly with CC in Google Labs . Google Labs is expanding CC from a personal agent into a collaborative group agent designed to handle household logistics and shared schedules. CC even gets its own email address to coordinate family calendars, track group to-dos, and streamline daily logistics in one spot with built-in privacy controls. CC for groups is now rolling out as an experimental preview in Google Labs.

Learn how AI breakthroughs accelerate science and improve lives . AI is transforming theoretical science into practical, everyday impact . By accelerating life-saving therapies, forecasting natural disasters, and personalizing education, our technology delivers tangible benefits worldwide. Today, Google tools support more than 300 languages spoken by 7 billion people — reaching 86% of the global population. By open-sourcing models like MedGemma and partnering with leading research institutions, we're helping scientists make discoveries faster to improve lives everywhere. Plus, new visualizations of our AI & Economy ATLAS data make it easier to see how AI is reshaping global work, including scientific research.

See how the future of AI computing could be in space . Project Suncatcher will launch its first test satellite with Planet to evaluate how Google TPUs perform under real space conditions. Satellites in low-Earth orbit can access up to eight times more solar power than on Earth, opening up new possibilities for long-term AI infrastructure. Learn questions we’re still exploring in our new four-part video series.

Pre-order Googlebook, the laptop of choice for Android users . Built on Android and paired with desktop foundations from ChromeOS, Googlebook is designed for Gemini Intelligence and engineered to work with your Android phone right out of the box. New on-device AI features like Magic Pointer let you point and ask Gemini about anything on your screen with a quick cursor wiggle, while Rambler smart voice dictation instantly structures verbal brain dumps into organized, shareable notes. With no-code custom widgets and background task processing, Googlebook simplifies your daily workflow so you can get more done effortlessly.

Check out WeatherNext 3, our most advanced and accurate global weather AI model . Our flagship AI weather forecasting model now includes real-time satellite data, hourly refreshes, higher resolution, precise precipitation forecasting, and clean energy variables. Plus, it’s now integrated across Search, Gemini, Maps, Google Maps Platform, and Cloud.

Explore AlphaGenome Atlas: a high-resolution map of human DNA . There are billions of possible mutations in the human genome — far too many to ever test in a lab. So we introduced AlphaGenome Atlas, a database that predicts the effects of every possible single nucleotide variant in the human genome, all 9 billion of them. Designed to require zero coding skills, it’s already accelerating real-world breakthroughs in rare disease research and complex genetics.

Track methane emissions globally from space . We partnered with NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory to develop MAPL-EMIT, a deep learning AI model that tracks global methane leaks from space. The model detects 50% more emissions than human experts and has already uncovered over 23,000 previously unmapped plumes, including 24 of the world's 25 largest-emitting landfills. All data is openly available on Google Earth Engine to help climate researchers and operators take faster action

See five amazing visuals of the male fruit fly’s brain map . Scientists at Google, HHMI Janelia, and Cambridge University have built the first complete brain map of an adult male fruit fly, charting over 166,000 neurons and nearly 12,000 distinct cell types with the help of Google AI. By stitching together millions of microscopic images into a navigable 3D model, this research uncovers how sensory cues transform into movement. It’s a breakthrough for neuroscience that brings us closer to understanding how complex brains function.

Learn about the new DeepMind Institute . The DeepMind Institute is a platform for researchers and thinkers from across Google DeepMind, Google, and the wider global research community to work on and publish creative, deeply informed ideas about a world with AGI. With AGI on the horizon, it’s incumbent on the creators of AI technology to sincerely and thoughtfully address its risks — but its transformative impact cannot be steered by technologists alone. DMI serves as a dedicated forum to spur debate, bring together diverse global voices, and build a consensus that ensures AGI benefits everyone.

Access fast help on your PC with the Gemini app for Windows . Now, using the Alt + Space shortcut, you can open Gemini any time over your work to fact-check docs or brainstorm ideas without breaking your stride. In the dedicated workspace, you can delegate multi-step tasks to Gemini Spark, synthesize files across Gmail and Drive, and generate Nano Banana images or Gemini Omni videos — all in one place.
